# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Brooks**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone]
[Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Security Health Plan — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or the address given when I call the number on the back of my insurance card]

**RE: Appeal of denial of prior authorization — Total hip replacement, CPT 27130**

- **Member name:** Rowan Brooks
- **Member ID:** W772624569
- **Reference number:** POC-A5F6D22435-38075
- **Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-07
- **Plan:** Security Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin
- **Governing policy:** eviCore CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-07/EviCore_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replac%20Arthro_Final_V2.0.2025_eff11.05.2025_pub07.22.2025.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which Security Health Plan denied on 2026-08-07 under reference number POC-A5F6D22435-38075. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria.

This appeal is timely. The denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-03**, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address has changed, I ask that this appeal be routed to the correct member appeals unit and that I be told where it was sent.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

The policy that governs this request, eviCore CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty, sets out an imaging requirement and a symptom requirement. I have quoted the plan's language below exactly as it appears, and matched each part to what is in my chart.

**1. The imaging requirement.**

The policy states:

> "Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

Among the findings the policy lists under the heading "Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis" is:

> "Tönnis Grade 2 - 3 osteoarthritis"

My imaging of 2026-06-09 was a weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph. It showed joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. These are the structural findings of advanced osteoarthritis on a weight-bearing film — narrowed joint space, sclerosis under the cartilage surface, and osteophyte formation, all documented together.

The denial notice does not tell me what the reviewer concluded about this radiograph, what grade was assigned, or which listed imaging finding the reviewer looked for and did not find. Because the notice gives no reasoning on that point, I am asking the plan to state plainly whether the 2026-06-09 weight-bearing radiograph was reviewed, how it was graded, and against which of the policy's listed imaging findings it was measured. If the plan's reviewer reached a different reading of this film than my surgeon did, I ask to be told what that reading was and who made it.

I would also note that the policy's imaging list is set out as alternatives — the plan's own word is "ANY" — so a single qualifying finding is sufficient under its terms. The other pathways in the policy, including "Imaging shows a fracture of the femoral head or femoral neck." with "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option.", and the findings "avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head" and "inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum with joint space narrowing", describe different conditions and are not the basis of my request. My request rests on the osteoarthritis pathway.

**2. The symptom requirement.**

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

The first is:

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall)for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document 24 months of progressive pain in the hip, unrelieved by rest. I walk with a cane and am limited to one block. I ask that the criterion quoted above be applied, as written, to those documented facts.

The second is:

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document that I cannot put on my shoes unassisted, that I require a cane to ambulate, and that my range of motion is limited by pain, with positive provocative testing on the affected side. Dressing myself and walking are basic daily activities, and my chart shows I cannot do them normally.

**3. Non-surgical management.**

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document supervised physical therapy directed at hip abductor strengthening and gait, 16 weeks from 2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14, with 16 visits completed, as recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-29 that gave three weeks of partial relief. My pain has continued and progressed despite all of it. I ask that the criterion quoted above be applied, as written, to that documented course of care.

The policy also sets out the following criteria exceptions, which I quote here so that the record of the governing language is complete: "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate." and "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate".

**4. Surgical readiness.**

The policy includes this note:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My chart documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

**One limitation I want to be transparent about.** Several of the criteria excerpts above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I have not been given in full. I am quoting only the policy language I have been able to obtain, and I have not put anything in quotation marks that I could not verify word for word. Where the policy lists additional conditions I cannot see, I am not attempting to characterize them, and I ask the plan to supply them.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

The plan holds the clinical review criteria used to make this decision, and I am asking for them in writing. Specifically, I request:

- the complete criteria set applied to CPT 27130 in my case, identified by title and version, including the full text of every list that the excerpts above introduce;
- confirmation of whether this request was reviewed under eviCore CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty, under Security Health Plan's own "Total Hip Replacement Surgery" policy maintained on its PolicyTech site, or under both;
- the specific criterion or criteria the reviewer found unmet, and the reviewer's reading of my 2026-06-09 weight-bearing radiograph;
- the name, credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination.

I mention the PolicyTech policy because I understand Security Health Plan maintains its own total hip replacement policy there. I also understand that the plan's "Back Surgical Procedures" and hip impingement policies now redirect to a Sanford Health login page that members cannot access. If any non-public document was used in deciding my case, I am requesting a copy of it in writing so that I can respond to the actual standard being applied to me.

## Closing

I am asking Security Health Plan to overturn the denial of 2026-08-07 and authorize the total hip replacement (CPT 27130) that Dr. Lindqvist has documented as necessary. My imaging, my symptom duration, my functional losses, and my completed course of provider-directed non-surgical care are all in the file, and I believe they meet the criteria the plan itself publishes. If the plan maintains this denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion not met and the evidence the reviewer relied on, along with information about my next level of appeal, including independent external review.

I am happy to provide any additional records. Please contact me at [phone] or [email].

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Brooks**
Member ID: W772624569
Reference number: POC-A5F6D22435-38075

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-07
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report, 2026-06-09, and images
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14, 16 visits)
- Injection record, 2026-03-29
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office wishes to include]
